rows.difficultyReason: Prove two specified triangle pairs similar using square and complementary-angle facts, then connect their corresponding side ratios through the common length AT to express the height.
rows.derivation: FCB and BAT have right angles and a second pair from CD parallel AB. TSA and AEB have right angles, while TAS and ABE are complementary to BAE. Correspondence gives AT=1/x and h/y=AT, hence h=y/x.

rows.difficultyReason: Use the supplied corresponding side lengths to obtain the scale factor, form and solve an equation for the unknown base, then calculate and round a triangle area.
rows.derivation: Scale 20/4=5; 5(2x-5)=7x+3 gives x=28/3, base 41/3 and area 82/3 square centimetres, rounding to 27 square centimetres.

rows.difficultyReason: Build on the scaffolded similarity and congruence proof to recognise the midpoint-of-hypotenuse property, then apply it twice after constructing an altitude in a fresh triangle.
rows.derivation: AA gives AMP similar ABC, so AP/AC=AM/AB=1/2. AP=PC and common PM with right angles yield congruent APM and CPM, hence AM=CM. Since AM=MB, joining CM gives two isosceles triangles. An altitude makes two right triangles; join its foot to each hypotenuse midpoint to obtain four isosceles triangles.
